transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-30 15:00 UTC
Length: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Eric Huang (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO, LucidStream), Maya Chen (Infra), Samir Gupta (PM)

Summary: quick discovery on whether LucidStream should start with Redwood hosted (PLG/self-serve) using credits to get to first token or go straight to Dedicated/Private VPC for production. Security and latency concerns surfaced; action items assigned.

[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. I see Alex, Maya, Samir in the room, and Priya from our infra team will run through the technical bits. Quick agenda: 1) understand your current stack and constraints, 2) time-to-first-token with our free credits, 3) hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC considerations, 4) security requirements. Sound good?
[00:18] Alex (CTO): Yeah sounds good. We have about 45 min — we are evaluating options, want to move fast but need to satisfy legal/security for certain customers.
[00:29] Priya (SE): awesome. Quick call-out: when people say "hosted" here we mean Redwood hosted API endpoints; "dedicated" is reserved GPU capacity in our infra, and "private" means the VPC/private deployment with customer-managed networking.
[00:43] Maya: just to flag — data residency and KMS integration are musts for a lot of our clients in EU. SOC2 also required.
[00:52] Jordan: totally — we have SOC2, and there's a private deployment path that can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and sits in your VPC. We'll share docs after the call.
[01:10] Samir (PM): high level, we're prototyping a support assistant and some classification features. Our goal is to get initial calls into prod for a handful of customers in Q1. So speed matters.
[01:25] Priya: for speed the PLG/self-serve hosted API is the fastest path — sign up, use free credits, get to first token in hours. But if you need for-prod isolation or strict KMS, Private deploy is the route.
[01:42] Jordan: can I ask what your target latency and QPS look like? That determines whether hosted is fine or you need dedicated pools.
[01:50] Alex: we'd be happy with p95 < 250ms for short chat flows, qps around 20–50 peak for alpha, maybe more later. Also cost sensitivity — we are a startup but enterprise customers will push cost expectations.
[02:10] Priya: okay that p95 at 250ms is achievable on hosted for a lot of our open-model configs for short contexts; if you push to long contexts or large batches, dedicated or private with specific kernel/quantization profiles will reduce per-token cost.
[02:30] Eric (SE): worth noting our runtime does continuous batching and prefix caching — you can reduce unit cost with small architectural changes. We can run a micro-benchmark during the pilot.
[02:45] Alex: micro-benchmark would be great. How fast do you usually do those?
[02:50] Priya: small bench can be 1–2 days for synthetic traces, 3–5 days to get representative numbers with your real prompts. We'll need a sample prompt set and traffic pattern.
[03:10] Maya: on security, we have a few questions: 1) SSO/SAML for user access to console and logs, 2) audit logs retention, 3) encryption — we require customer-managed keys for anything PII.
[03:24] Jordan: yes SSO via SAML/Okta supported, RBAC in the console, and audit logs exportable. Private deployment supports KMS/HSM; hosted can do envelope encryption but not customer-managed keys unless we go Dedicated with a private control plane.
[03:45] Samir: ok, explain the free credits flow and what we can realistically evaluate inside the credits.
[03:52] Jordan: free credits are intended to get you to first meaningful metrics — sample app, up to X tokens (we'll send exact numbers). They cover hosted usage; they can also be used to spin up a small dedicated pool for short evals if we agree. Typically teams check throughput, latency, and cost per inference and then decide.
[04:15] Alex: if credits only cover hosted, can we test a dedicated config during evaluation?
[04:20] Jordan: yes — we can apply credits against a dedicated pilot for a short window but that requires a bit of setup and an SE handoff. Priya will own that.
[04:32] Priya: the setup for a tiny dedicated pool is ~2–4 days of work to provision and validate, depending on cloud region and instance types, plus model onboarding. For Private VPC it can be longer because of network and KMS provisioning — usually 1–2 weeks minimum.
[04:50] Alex: good to know. Also, do you do canary rollouts across model versions, and can we pin model versions for compliance?
[04:59] Eric: yes, you can pin model versions, use rollouts and A/B experiments in the console, and we keep model and inference logs for regressions — retention depends on your plan, enterprise has longer retention.
[05:14] Samir: what's the typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.
[05:20] Jordan: hosted has more variable per-token unit cost; dedicated amortizes GPU cost so for steady high QPS you can be 30–60% cheaper depending on model and quantization. We'll show a worked example in the pricing sheet.
[05:36] Alex: any gotchas for streaming/chat vs batch embedding workloads?
[05:42] Priya: streaming chat has stricter latency SLOs and benefits from lower-batch sizes; embeddings are cheaper in batch and can be run on different hardware. We recommend separating routes so you can optimize per workload.
[06:00] [Speaker 1 — partial transcription]: um yeah, and for the KV cache, does the redwood runtime persist that across requests or is it ephemeral?
[06:10] Priya: KV cache is per-session and can be cached across requests in our runtime; when you pin a session you get faster subsequent tokens. For private deployments you can choose to persist caches to your own object store if needed.
[06:28] Alex: let's talk compliance docs — can you share SOC2 report and a short security pack?
[06:35] Jordan: yes, will share SOC2 and a private deployment security pack. Link in chat: https://redwood.example.com/sales/lucidstream/sec-pack (placeholder).
[06:48] Maya: on KMS — does Redwood require us to expose keys to Redwood? We cannot do that for some customers.
[06:55] Eric: no — for Private deployments the keys remain in your KMS and we call them from inside the VPC; for hosted we use envelope encryption. We'll outline limitations in the checklist.
[07:10] Samir: timeline question — if we commit to a pilot today, what's the soonest we can run something realistic?
[07:18] Priya: hosted with credits: same day provisioning and you can start in hours. Tiny dedicated pilot: 2–4 days. Private VPC pilot: 1–2 weeks for full KMS & network.
[07:35] Alex: our preference is start hosted to validate UX, then follow with a private pilot for customers with compliance needs. Works for us.
[07:44] Jordan: that's a common path: PLG/prove value, then lock down a private deployment for regulated customers.
[07:50] Priya: any specific traffic patterns or prompts we should be aware of today?
[07:55] Alex: the flows are 2–6 turn chats, average prompt length ~150 tokens, sometimes retrieval augmented generation (RAG) with 4–8 doc snippets.
[08:08] Eric: RAG workloads mean you need to consider embedding routes and vector DB calls. We can help quantify end-to-end latency.
[08:17] Maya: regarding VPC peering, we run in GCP — any preferred regions for Redwood infra?
[08:22] Jordan: we support major regions; we'll match region and instance types to your proximity. For latency-sensitive customers we recommend regional dedicated pools.
[08:36] [00:09:00 approximate marker] Samir: who are the internal stakeholders we need from your side?
[08:42] Jordan: for pilot: AE (me), SE (Priya/Eric), and Solutions Architect as needed. For private deploy legal/security will be engaged.
[08:50] Alex: legal will want a draft DPA and a list of sub-processors — can you provide that?
[08:57] Jordan: yes, the DPA and subprocessor list will be in the security pack we share.
[09:10] [00:10:00] Maya: small nit — network egress costs for embeddings can be big; is there a recommended architecture to minimize egress?
[09:20] Priya: keep embedding compute in-region and colocate vector DB; use batching and local caching. For private deployment egress is minimized since compute lives in your VPC.
[09:35] Alex: what about model selection — are you providing model catalogs or do we bring our own?
[09:42] Eric: we have a model catalog with open models and Redwood-verified profiles; you can also bring your own model artifacts for private deployments. Quantization/optimization help is available.
[09:55] Samir: curious if you support instrumented A/B tests to compare models in production?
[10:02] Jordan: yes — rollouts and A/B are supported in the console. We also have quality monitoring and can alert on regression vs your prompt set.
[10:12] [Speaker labels swap briefly] Speaker 2 (auto): so are there any limits to the free credits?
[10:19] Jordan: credits are time- and token-limited; we'll put exact allocation in the email. They are intended for quick validation not sustained production.
[10:30] Maya: legal follow-up: do we have to sign any enterprise contract to access dedicated pilot?
[10:36] Jordan: for small dedicated pilots we can do a short pilot agreement; enterprise contracts only required for long-term reserved capacity.
[10:45] Alex: ok let's try to align a 4-week pilot: week 0 baseline hosted quickstart + bench, week 1 dedicated pilot (if needed) micro-bench, week 2 private prep if required, week 3 decision and run to alpha. Is that realistic?
[10:59] Priya: yes that's realistic if you can provide prompts and sample traffic. We'll need security contacts early for private path.
[11:10] Samir: do you have runbooks for failover and graceful degradation? Our SLAs require fallbacks to smaller models when capacity spikes.
[11:18] Eric: we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies — you can configure model variants per route for graceful degradation.
[11:30] Alex: one last thing on cost controls — can we limit tokens per request and cap daily spend via API keys?
[11:36] Jordan: yes, token limits per route and API-key level quota controls exist; we also have per-token cost dashboards.
[11:45] [auto note] Shared artifacts referenced: pilot-pricing-template.xlsx, private-deploy-checklist.pdf, security-pack (SOC2+subprocessors). Links will be provided in follow-up.
[11:55] Maya: thanks — this is helpful. Can you also send an example of a minimal infra diagram for the private deploy?
[12:02] Priya: yes — we'll attach a diagram and the VPC peering checklist.
[12:10] Jordan: recap of next steps — Jordan sends pricing/pilot sheet, Priya shares VPC + KMS checklist and we get security contacts from Alex. Customer to confirm timeline by 2028-12-04. Any blockers?
[12:25] Alex: none from our side, thanks.
[12:30] Jordan: great, thanks all. We'll follow up with links and items by EOD.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few speaker labels were auto-assigned; some proper nouns might be slightly off (e.g., "Red wood" vs Redwood).
